Priya K: Quick update — ran perf + FlameGraph on CPU side for tokenization/scheduler overhead during a 2k-token generation workload. Dumped perf.data and generated flame.svg. Key commands:

Priya K: ```sudo perf record -F 99 -g -- python3 -m rwinf.server --workload=regen_test
perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

Priya K: Initial read: Python interpreter + GIL scheduling shows ~28% of samples, tokenization C-extension ~12%, batching logic in py async scheduler ~18%, syscall wait/epoll ~9%.

Alex M: Nice. Can you paste the top stacks (folded) snippet?

Priya K: pasted small sample:
```
python3;_PyEval_EvalFrameEx;Tokenizer.tokenize;Tokenizer.c_tokenize 120
python3;uvloop.loop.run_forever;Scheduler._schedule_batch 85
python3;_socket.recv;KVCache.fetch 40
```

Sam T: So tokenizer c code is nontrivial. Is the C-ext locked on GIL during heavy loops? :thinking:

Priya K: Yep, the C-ext currently acquires GIL for small chunks; we see a lot of time in _PyEval overhead. Might refactor to release GIL around bulk memcpy.

Riley P: How big were the batch sizes? Could batching heuristics be causing extra scheduler overhead?

Priya K: Test used dynamic batching target 64 tokens, average batch latency ~85ms. When I forced fixed batch of 16, scheduler overhead dropped 10% but kernel utilization fell.

infra-bot: perf run complete: profile saved to s3://perf-bench/1749801234/perf.data :white_check_mark:

Alex M: Can you run with PERF_RECORD_PER_THREAD (or -a) to separate thread samples? Might isolate IO waits.

Priya K: Good call — next run will collect per-thread. Also going to run with python -Xfaulthandler off and try building tokenizer with nogil branch.

Sam T: Also consider using BPF/tracepoint for uvloop timers — could show scheduler wakeups.

Priya K: Agreed. Next steps: run per-thread perf, generate diff flamegraphs between nogil tokenizer vs master, and submit a small change to release GIL around memcopy. I'll post results tomorrow.

Alex M: :thumbsup: thanks.

Riley P: If you need a quick harness, I have a script that replays workloads at scale — ping me.
